Skipper-CCD background rejection with sideband patch anomalies

CODEX · gpt-6-astra · high effort · fixed chronological holdout

On 22 held-out acquisitions, a 32×32-pixel Isolation Forest region mask retains 81.91% of effective exposure and reduces the reconstructed 4–7 electron background-rate proxy by 78.57%. The largest improvement is concentrated in one module/quadrant. This result is relative to an active-geometry baseline, not the existing production cleaning pipeline.

Dataset and baseline

All 218 files are usable under the declared geometry/calibration checks: 109 acquisition IDs, two modules, four HDUs per file, 515×3200 stored pixels. Active geometry is 512×3072 pixels/HDU. The full baseline is 135.610 million pixel-days and 102,112 ROI clusters. Nominal EXPOSURE is zero; effective exposure accumulates during approximately 4.77 hours of readout. Raw FITS bytes are external and SHA-256 indexed in data/manifest.json.

Subtract the median reverse overscan per row and fit the 0/1-electron peaks for gain. The ROI is 3.5 ≤ reconstructed cluster charge < 7.5 e⁻: integer bins 4,5,6,7. Clusters are 8-connected pixels above 0.7 e⁻; charge is their above-threshold sum. Accept a whole pre-reconstructed cluster according to its maximum-charge pixel’s tile. No reclustering is performed after masking.

Independent method selection

The primary contribution is an unsupervised multivariate patch classifier. Its six inputs summarize low-charge sideband clusters, occupied pixels of high-charge clusters, negative tails, temporal persistence and local neighborhoods. It never receives target-event counts or positions. All clusters with charge 2.5–20 e⁻ are excluded from positive diagnostic channels, including their individual pixels.

Three primary families were tested: dynamic robust scores, combined persistent/dynamic robust scores, and Isolation Forest. Static sideband occupancy and single-channel scores are comparison methods; none is a rewrite of the production masks. Robust PCA, Laplacian cosmic-ray cleaning and autoencoders were considered but not implemented: their extra assumptions or focus on individual events were not justified by this task. METHOD.md records these decisions and references.

Validation protocol

Train: IDs22–86 (65 acquisitions). Validation: 87–108 (22). Test: 109–130 (22). Paired modules and all eight HDUs stay together. The data contain one paired end-timestamp discrepancy, so grouping uses shared image ID rather than exact timestamp matching. Hyperparameters are selected on validation only: maximize F_equal among primary candidates with f_exp ≥ 0.8. Thresholds are training-exposure-weighted score quantiles, applied absolutely to later images.

The chosen Forest has 100 trees, 256 samples/tree, six features, seed 20260927 and threshold 0.513326711. Selection was committed as 1812e3f before opening test ROI results. Validation retained 0.8280 with r_B=0.2418; test retains 0.8191 with r_B=0.2143. Test operating curves and ablations are descriptive and did not alter selection.

S101 HDU0 supplies most of the baseline ROI excess and most of the rejection. Its retained fraction is much lower than the global retained fraction; a pooled 80% constraint is not an 80% constraint per quadrant. This needs to be acceptable to a future experimental signal model before adopting the cut. Sideband persistence between training halves is measured in results/persistence.csv; acquisition histories and dynamic feature ablations probe transient behavior.

Negative result: removing the negative-tail or neighborhood feature improves the matched-budget Forest on both validation and test; the six-feature descriptor is not established as optimal. Removing persistence or high-charge information worsens rejection. These diagnostic ablations were run after the primary configuration was frozen and the test was opened, so they are reported without replacing the final selection. A new independent dataset is needed to confirm a revised smaller descriptor.

Five synthetic/analytic unit checks pass. A separate graph-walk implementation checks connected components; arithmetic-series exposure and direct event loops reproduce the final counts and exposure. Removing 941 actual ROI clusters from all eight HDUs of test acquisition109 leaves every diagnostic feature exactly unchanged. Isolated synthetic 4–7 e⁻ injections also leave the feature maps unchanged. Exposure-weighted simulated signal anchors survive with fraction 0.81772 (binomial standard error 0.00122), consistent with f_exp; this does not measure reconstruction efficiency.

Randomly translating each HDU’s mask yields a median rate ratio 0.840, with a central 95% range [0.761, 0.922], compared with the aligned mask’s 0.214. This is a spatial-alignment control, not a p-value: it preserves HDU-specific mask areas and those HDUs have different rates. Negative-tail-only rejection is weak; static sideband and robust scores underperform the selected Forest under the declared validation exposure constraint. These results and every tested point remain in CSV outputs.

Physical interpretation and limitations

For N ROI events and exposure E, B=N/E, f_exp=E1/E0 and r_B=B1/B0. The auxiliary F_equal=f_exp/r_B does not replace the Pareto curve. For a spatially uniform signal proportional to pixel-days, unchanged efficiency and a known background in the Gaussian counting regime, S=sE and Z≈S/√N=s√(E/B), giving Z1/Z0=√F_equal. This is only a conditional sensitivity proxy. Readout-induced or collision-correlated signals can violate that exposure model.

The rate normalization assumes a uniform readout clock and zero initial integration. The baseline lacks production masks; residual backgrounds, edge effects, merged clusters, readout transients and calibration-model imperfections remain. The study does not establish a physical background mechanism, true interaction-charge spectrum, mass exposure, extended-signal efficiency, or generalization to another detector/campaign. The paired four-acquisition bootstrap does not cover calibration, geometry or selection systematics, and may miss longer correlations. Reconstruction stress checks hold the trained mask fixed. Some calibration fits have reduced chi-square above unity; gain/noise metadata are published for scrutiny.

Reproducibility and provenance

Set SKIPPER_DATA_DIR to the directory containing the 218 pp_proc FITS files, install requirements.txt in a Python 3.13 environment (observed: 3.13.5), then run:

SKIPPER_DATA_DIR=/path/to/pp_proc bash CODEX/gpt-6-astra_high/reproduce.sh

The workflow verifies input hashes, reconstructs the baseline and catalogs from FITS, fits development models, regenerates the held-out evaluation, runs numerical/stress checks, and rebuilds every figure and this report. No FITS data or caches belong in Git. The data downloader accepts an owner-supplied Google Drive URL/ID; none was provided, so no public dataset link is invented. README.md gives full setup and data instructions.

All scientific code was written for this run. Astropy reads FITS; SciPy fits calibration peaks and labels components; scikit-learn supplies Isolation Forest; NumPy performs array arithmetic; Matplotlib generates figures and the PDF. Parent MOSKITA code was read only for geometry/calibration/exposure conventions. No parent code is imported. Every figure is generated by src/report.py; PROVENANCE.md maps outputs to source functions, configuration, libraries and checks. The HTML embeds every figure and is portable as one file.

Session turn_context and local configuration agree on gpt-6-astra, high effort; a more specific backend snapshot is unavailable. ORIGINAL_PROMPT.md is verbatim. This run supplies separate verification calculations but no independent human or different-model review. The repository started on an unborn Claude-named branch; Codex created its own branch and did not alter CLAUDE/.
